definition: A defined sequence of steps, tools and decisions that an AI system executes to complete a larger goal.
details: A workflow chains models with data sources, tools and human-approval gates. In agentic workflows the model chooses the next step dynamically, while deterministic workflows run a fixed script — the two ends of the automation spectrum.

explainer.lead: A workflow is a defined sequence of steps, tools and decisions an AI system executes to complete a larger goal. It matters because it is how models become dependable, repeatable systems rather than one-off calls.

tiers.eli5: It's a recipe for the AI: do this, then that, check with a human, then finish.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers chain models with data sources, tools and human-approval gates, choosing between dynamic and fixed scripts; a pitfall is picking the wrong end of that spectrum for the task.
tiers.paperLevel: A workflow chains models with data sources, tools and human-approval gates; agentic workflows let the model choose the next step dynamically, while deterministic workflows run a fixed script, the two ends of the automation spectrum.

explainer.example: A document pipeline extracts data with a model, checks it through a human-approval gate, then files it—each step fixed in advance.
